class.name: NetwDisplayOffset
class.brief_description: One display channel's render offset, the residual that holds a visual still while the thing it displays jumps.
class.description:
A correction or a change of display source moves the value under the visual in one frame. Writing that through would be seen as a step, so the difference is kept here as an OFFSET, composed back onto every write and decayed toward nothing, which turns the step into a glide. The offset holds at most one residual, and it is the outstanding part of every jump absorbed so far. A new absorption composes onto what has not decayed yet rather than replacing it, because replacing it hands the screen exactly the part of the previous jump the viewer had not been shown. [codeblock] offset.arm(true) # the display source changed var shown = offset.apply(target, glide, limit, last_written, mode)
offset.absorb(correction_delta, limit) # a reconciliation landed var shown = offset.apply(target, glide, limit, last_written, mode)
offset.clear() # a teleport should be SEEN [/codeblock] Four value shapes carry an offset: [float], [Vector2], [Vector3] and [Quaternion]. Anything else holds none, so its writes pass through untouched. [b]Note:[/b] a [float] channel in [constant NetwInterpolate.MODE_ANGLE] takes its residual the short way around the circle, which is the only place the mode changes what an offset is.

method.name: absorb
method.description: Absorbs one correction: [param recovery] is how far the displayed thing MOVED, so the offset takes its negation and the visual stays where it was. Composed onto whatever is still held, then clamped to [param limit]. Disarms, because an absorbed jump is not a source change.

method.name: apply
method.description: Answers what to write this frame: [param target] with the held offset composed onto it, after decaying that offset by [param glide]. An armed offset seeds itself here rather than at the arming, because [param target] is the first value the new source has produced and the residual is measured against it: the offset becomes [param displayed] relative to [param target], clamped to [param limit], and the arming is spent. An offset decayed to nothing is dropped, so the channel returns to writing [param target] exactly.

method.name: arm
method.description: Arms or disarms the seed. An armed offset measures itself at the next [method apply] and holds the displayed value still while the new source takes over.

method.name: clear
method.description: Drops the held offset and the arming both, which is what makes the next write land on the raw value. A genuine desync should be seen to snap, so a teleport clears rather than absorbs.

method.name: held
method.description: The outstanding residual, or [code]null[/code] when none is held.

method.name: is_armed
method.description: Whether the next [method apply] seeds an offset from the value it is given.

method.name: is_held
method.description: Whether a residual is outstanding. False both before the first jump and after the last one has decayed away.
